paper: Anderson dispatches and Foster letter carried north
route: Fort Sumter -> Charleston -> Washington; intermediate path not established
limits: Receipt of paper is not an exact personal arrival. The 6 April order places Talbot in Washington by then. No named permanent carrier office.

paper: Communication about the Shannon firing and nearby cutter
arrival: 1861-04-04 Charleston; same-day return through Fort Johnson
route: Fort Sumter -> Charleston -> Fort Johnson -> Fort Sumter
limits: Date follows Foster letter of 5 April describing yesterday [I]. Local boat trip, not the onward Washington journey.

paper: Charter authority to Tompkins and instructions to H. L. Scott
route: Washington -> New York; intermediate route unknown
limits: Both papers expressly name Fox as bearer. Letter date is not proof of departure. Recipient posts absent.

paper: Presidential notice of the provision attempt to Pickens and Beauregard
route: Washington -> Charleston; outward intermediate stations not stated; return via Florence and Richmond
limits: Joint journey, not serial handoffs. Chew read and handed the notice; Pickens then read and handed it to Beauregard. Talbot was refused entry to Sumter. Return: Charleston 8 April 23:00 -> Washington 12 April morning.

paper: Separate sealed presidential dispatch for Anderson, returned undelivered
arrival: NOT DELIVERED to Anderson; Washington return 1861-04-12 morning
route: Washington -> Charleston -> Florence -> Richmond -> Washington
limits: Do not turn the successful notice to Pickens into delivery of this sealed paper to Anderson.

paper: Pickens letter to Davis and packet to Walker
route: Charleston -> Confederate government at Montgomery; intermediate path unknown
limits: Paper calls Hayne an aide and trustworthy return bearer. Neither actual departure nor receipt is dated. Surname not expanded.

paper: First demand for evacuation; Anderson answer carried back
names_as_read: James Chesnut, Jr.; Stephen D. Lee; A. R. Chisolm
arrival: 1861-04-11 15:45 Fort Sumter; return city 17:10 after departure fort 16:40
route: Charleston -> Fort Sumter -> Charleston; flag of truce
limits: Three joint bearers, not three successive offices. Same-day boat classification is [I] from the harbor journey; no exact vessel named in this report.

paper: Second communication and conditional evacuation reply
names_as_read: James Chesnut, Jr.; Stephen D. Lee; Colonel Chisolm; Mr. Pryor
route: Charleston -> Fort Sumter; subsequent leg to Fort Johnson in C09
limits: Chesnut/Lee sign the detailed report; Foster p.18 lists four visitors and rounds arrival to01:00. Preserve both observations; companions are not serial bearers. Reply received 03:15. Negotiation time is not a compliance hold.

paper: Notice of fire and order to James at Fort Johnson
names_as_read: James Chesnut, Jr.; Stephen D. Lee
route: Fort Sumter -> Fort Johnson -> Charleston headquarters about daylight
limits: 03:20 is the notice time, not an independently timed boat departure. James is the recipient, not a bearer. Fort Johnson recipient post not declared.

paper: Initial offers of assistance after fire and loss of flag
names_as_read: Colonel Miles; Colonel Pryor; Captain Lee
route: Beauregard headquarters -> Fort Sumter; path not detailed
limits: Beauregard names these aides as the first group. Do not replace them with later visitors or infer a single continuous chain.

paper: Terms of evacuation after white flag
route: Beauregard headquarters -> Fort Sumter; path not detailed
limits: Second group named by Beauregard. Do not expand Allston or Jones into unsupported identities. Written confirmation dated 17:55; its own bearer is not named.

paper: Simons inquiry about surrender, with contested authority and terms
names_as_read: Colonel Wigfall; Private Gourdin Young; two unnamed oarsmen in joint report
departure: 1861-04-13 after flag fell; exact departure unknown
arrival: Fort Sumter time unknown; back at Morris Island 14:15 in Simons report
route: Morris Island -> Fort Sumter -> Morris Island -> report at Charleston
limits: Simons says he sent Wigfall; do not call this a direct presidential or Beauregard instruction. His unconditional-surrender account conflicts with Anderson formal terms. No forced successful authority.

paper: Offer of firefighting assistance after the Morris Island report
names_as_read: James Chesnut, Jr.; John L. Manning; A. R. Chisolm
arrival: 1861-04-13 Fort Sumter; return report Charleston about 19:00
route: Charleston -> steamer Osiris -> small boat/embrasure Fort Sumter -> Charleston
limits: A distinct later visit. The report is dated 15 April describing the 13th; no precise outward time.

paper: Fleet inquiry about surrender and evacuation transport
route: Fleet -> boat -> Morris Island; requested onward visit to Fort Moultrie
limits: Oral inquiry; permission and an answer next day were discussed, not a completed journey to Fort Moultrie. Name not expanded.

paper: Whiting-signed dispatch about Marcy inquiry
route: Morris Island -> Beauregard; intermediate path unknown
limits: Exact identity join to Colonel Allston in C11 is held. Dispatch date is contextual, not a dated receipt.

paper: 12 March Army landing order, naval carriage legs
names_as_read: T. A. M. Craven (Crusader); Captain Walker (Brooklyn)
departure: Crusader original departure unknown; transfer to Walker 1861-03-26 Key West
arrival: Order received by Vogdes night 1861-03-31; Brooklyn back off Pensacola 1861-03-31
route: Washington/New York opening leg unresolved -> Crusader -> Key West -> Brooklyn -> Pensacola
limits: March 11 order promises an unnamed government bearer. Ward is expressly bearer of the Navy order to Craven, not established as bearer of the Army order. Do not invent the opening leg. Adams April1 refusal is a separate return paper. Addressee Vogdes is not the ship post holder Adams; destination-post binding is held.

paper: Welles order of 11 March to Craven (supporting delivery)
arrival: unknown; Welles12 March reports sending the order11 March, not its receipt
route: Navy Department -> Commander Craven; recipient location not specified on bearer line
limits: Welles says he sent it yesterday by Ward. Actual departure not equated to that statement. Separate from C16 Army paper.

paper: Welles 6 April order to Adams to cooperate in landing
arrival: Pensacola about midnight 1861-04-10; squadron delivery about noon 1861-04-12
route: Washington -> Aquia Creek -> Richmond -> near Atlanta -> Pensacola -> Wyandotte reached11 April -> offshore squadron12 April; conveyance on12 unnamed
limits: 1865 retrospective journey account: destroyed written dispatches near Atlanta and delivered substance. Wind prevented offshore passage 11 April. Return began Pensacola evening12; arrested near Montgomery13, per April15 letter. Weather/capture are not resistance.

paper: Confidential instructions to McCauley and Pendergrast
route: Washington -> Norfolk; first journey route and actual dates not established in pages used
limits: Two letters explicitly name Paulding bearer. Do not substitute his later Pawnee expedition for the first visit.

paper: Instructions to prepare Merrimack presented with engineer orders
arrival: Sunday following 12 April, at Portsmouth [1861-04-14 by calendar, I]
route: Washington -> Portsmouth/Norfolk navy yard; intermediate path unknown
limits: Isherwood April18 report says he presented orders and letter to McCauley. Do not silently identify that letter as the separately dated 13 April version.

paper: General-in-Chief letter dated 21 April to Patterson
route: Washington -> Philadelphia; path of messenger unknown
limits: Patterson describes a proposed troop route via Susquehanna and Annapolis; that is not evidence Palmer used it. Initials not expanded.

paper: Scott letter and verbal messages to Patterson
route: Washington -> Patterson; actual intermediate path and delivery time unknown
limits: Scott April29 says he wrote by Porter on27; paper date is not proved departure. Full identity remains held.

paper: Butler dispatches to Scott
route: Butler command -> Washington; departure point and path not specified in acknowledgment
limits: Scott April29 acknowledgment. Do not merge bearer Colonel Butler with addressee Brigadier-General Butler or expand surname.

paper: Davis dispatches to Lincoln under flag of truce
names_as_read: Col. Thos. H. Taylor; escort officer and twelve men unnamed
arrival: by 1861-07-09, paper transmitted to President; personal audience NOT established
route: Manassas -> McDowell command at Arlington -> General-in-Chief -> President; return ordered morning9
limits: Cover requests personal delivery; McDowell July9 says paper went through General-in-Chief. Not an authored situation in the inventoried pack: comparison evidence only.

paper: Patterson dispatches delivered to command at Cumberland
route: Patterson command -> Cumberland; actual path unknown
limits: The author own march via Grafton is not Closson itinerary. Comparison evidence only; do not force this paper into the McDowell advance notice.

paper: Commissioners sealed request for interview delivered at State Department
route: Commissioners in Washington -> State Department; local path unknown
limits: Seward memorandum says intended personal delivery to Secretary, actually received by Assistant Secretary. It does not name that assistant. Initials not expanded.

paper: Seward memorandum of15 March and8 April covering direction
departure: collected1861-04-08 State Department; exact departure unknown
arrival: by1861-04-09 commissioners acknowledgment; exact delivery date not stated
route: State Department -> commissioners in Washington; local path unknown
limits: Commissioners April9 acknowledgment names their secretary Pickett. Memorandum says delayed external delivery was with commissioners consent; it had already been submitted to President. No presidential incoming hold or resistant carrier is proved.

paper: Cadwalader written return to habeas writ
arrival: 1861-05-27 shortly after11:00, circuit court room Baltimore
route: Fort McHenry -> court at Masonic Hall Baltimore; intermediate path unknown
limits: Source says Lee appeared carrying return and had no instructions beyond delivery. No identity expansion to another Lee. Spicer issued writ, not established as its bearer. This is a paper to the court, not a proved delivery to Lincoln.

paper: Attempt to serve attachment; return signed by marshal
names_as_read: Washington Bonifant, in signed first-person return
arrival: 1861-05-28 outer gate Fort McHenry; NOT SERVED
route: Marshal/court -> Fort McHenry outer gate; no admitted delivery
limits: Attribute the journey to the signed reported return, not an independently established personal itinerary. A discovered newspaper/deputy lead remains unverified; no Vance fact asserted. Institutional signature alone does not settle who physically went. No live delivery draft.
